exp_info.description: This was one of the first real jobs in my life. I translated legal documents from Bulgarian into English as well as informal texts from English into Bulgarian. I learned how to work with programmes such as SDL Trados and saw how the translation process goes. This job made me realize that translation was not in my field of interest...

Then I got a job as an interpreter for a Chinese businessman who was doing training in one Bulgarian bike company. There I learned a lot of useful Chinese words and expressions as well as many bicycle terms. Since then I had been working sporadically as an interpreter for various events. In addition, I have also taken Chinese tourists on guided tours around Plovdiv. This experience allowed me to gain more confidence when working with people from different countries.

After I finished my B.A. degree, I did a one-year internship in Spain as an English Teaching Assistant. My responsibilities were mainly to help students work on their speaking skills. I was preparing interesting games, activities and was having casual conversations with them. By the end of the school year, many of the students had improved their level of English tremendously. Meanwhile, I managed to learn Spanish simply by listening and speaking - without any courses, schools or books.

This experience made me realize how important listening, speaking and a good environment are when learning a new language. That’s why I decided to start with the project Language Inspiration. My main objective is to prove that everybody can learn a new language with fun, joy and inspiration. All of my videos, articles and lessons are designed with a single purpose in mind - to show you that learning languages is fun, interesting and easy. You can also learn five languages.

All of this searching led me to London where I began to explore and put into practice my ideas. The first place that I came across was a private school for English lessons. I started teaching English to groups of adults. I incorporated a lot of games, funny dialogues and interesting activities on the lessons. Although most of the students were complete beginners, they relaxed and felt comfortable enough to start speaking in English. Their progress was immediately visible.

At the same time, I was working in a bilingual private nursery that was applying the Montessori teaching techniques. This allowed me to observe closely how the young children learn a language. The first-hand experience inspired me to come up with more ideas and methods to speed up the learning process. I understood that one of the key factors is to get a lot of input and individual attention. To have somebody who is always next to you explaining the words in your environment patiently.

All of my previously accumulated knowledge and experience are now part of my teaching style. My lessons, both online and in-person, are designed to help the students become confident when expressing themselves in another language. That is why I speak mainly in the target language allowing them to get a lot of input. I intend to prove that everybody can speak a new language even if they know only a few words. Be alchemists! Do the best out of what you have!

How much time have you spent learning English at school, university or private lessons? A lot? Far too much?

Great, because I have an offer for you. This time we will do things differently. Instead of focusing all of our efforts and attention on understanding grammar, we will use it as a tool to help us see how English actually works.

What do I mean by this?

During the lessons, we will speak ONLY in English by covering various topics - food, travelling, favorite movies, future plans, past experiences, etc. While talking about them, I will observe your manner of speaking. Once I notice a certain type of mistake that you keep making, I will explain how the grammar works in this case. We will practice as long as you need to fully grasp it. Then, we will continue with our conversation until we encounter another grammar concept that you need to work on.

Instead of trying to learn grammar and then put it into use, we find real-life situations where grammar has been already applied and intend to understand why and how it works.

I would love to talk to you soon. Until then smile, have fun and learn English.
